title: Employer Handbook: The Taxable Wage Base and Excess Wages
content:
For every financing class of the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts the taxable wage base is USD 14000.00: the wages paid to each employee in a calendar year that are subject to contributions. Wages an employee earns above that figure in the same calendar year are excess wages, measured per employee and cumulatively over the calendar year.

| Financing class | Taxable wage base (USD) | How excess wages are measured |
|---|---|---|
| Contributory — New Employer Standard Rate | 14000.00 | Per employee, cumulative over the calendar year |
| Contributory — New Employer Construction Rate | 14000.00 | Per employee, cumulative over the calendar year |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Positive Reserve | 14000.00 | Per employee, cumulative over the calendar year |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve | 14000.00 | Per employee, cumulative over the calendar year |
| Contributory — Delinquent Reporting Assigned Rate | 14000.00 | Per employee, cumulative over the calendar year |
| Reimbursing — Nonprofit Organization | 14000.00 | Per employee, cumulative over the calendar year |
| Reimbursing — Governmental Entity | 14000.00 | Per employee, cumulative over the calendar year |

## What "cumulative over the calendar year" means

The wage base is not a quarterly allowance. Each employee's wages are added up from 1 January; once that running total passes USD 14000.00, every further dollar paid to that employee in the same calendar year is excess. The count starts again on 1 January of the next year.

**Worked illustration (hypothetical employee, USD 5000.00 paid each quarter of one calendar year).**

| Quarter | Wages paid | Running total for the year | Within the wage base | Excess wages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First | 5000.00 | 5000.00 | 5000.00 | 0.00 |
| Second | 5000.00 | 10000.00 | 5000.00 | 0.00 |
| Third | 5000.00 | 15000.00 | 4000.00 | 1000.00 |
| Fourth | 5000.00 | 20000.00 | 0.00 | 5000.00 |

Across the year this employee contributes USD 14000.00 of wages within the base and USD 6000.00 of excess wages.

**Basis Q&A.** *Does a second employee share the first employee's wage base?* No. The base is measured for each employee separately; a business with several employees applies USD 14000.00 to each of them.
